subject: Intake: audit log sampling, retention buckets, and BYOK exception path
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Long <sarah.long@medivault.com>, procurement@medivault.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Intake: audit log sampling, retention buckets, and BYOK exception path

Sarah — thanks for the intake form. A few of our teams (product + infra + security) are on copy to triage.

High level from your form: Medivault needs longer audit retention for a subset of events (12 months), an option to provide a BYOK flow for a limited set of tenants, and the ability to request an audit-log sampling export on-demand for regulatory audits. You attached a list of required evidence; I’ve pulled that into the thread. (Attachment: requested_evidence_list.pdf)

Can you confirm two narrow things before we triage: 1) Is the 12-month retention required for all logs or only admin/audit events? 2) For BYOK, do you need client-managed keys for all environments or only production?

Next steps: I’ll open a triage channel internally to map options (sampling vs full retention), feasibility of BYOK for a pilot, and whether an exception + roadmap slot is the right path. Can someone from product/engineering provide rough dev estimates once we align on scope?

Thanks — Tessa

-- 
Tessa Morgan
Head of Security Programs
Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0123

From: Sarah Long <sarah.long@medivault.com>

Subject: Re: Intake: audit log sampling, retention buckets, and BYOK exception path

Thanks Tessa — quick answers:
1) 12 months applies to admin/audit events and any logs with user-identifiable actions; application-level telemetry can stay at your default (90 days).
2) BYOK is required for production only for now; staging/dev can use Redwood-managed keys.

We can share procurement windows after the legal review — I included procurement@medivault.com to coordinate. We’re happy to start with a pilot on a single customer segment if that makes it feasible.

Regards,
Sarah

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intake: audit log sampling, retention buckets, and BYOK exception path

Looping in some quick feasibility notes from infra:

- Retention: We can implement per-event-type retention buckets (90d default / 180d / 365d) with ~2 workstreams: storage lifecycle + query layer tagging. Storage cost scales with retention length; sampling exports reduce cost but add complexity to audit requests.

- Sampling/export: We can build an on-demand sampled export that preserves order and includes context, but it must be rate-limited and gated behind an admin flow (audit approvals). For regulatory audits that require full-fidelity logs, sampling may not be acceptable. Need legal/compliance confirmation on acceptability.

- BYOK (production-only pilot): BYOK for a tenant requires key wrapping + KMS integration and changes to our key-rotation and backup flows. Two options: 1) full BYOK where the tenant holds the root key (higher engineering surface, more compliance), or 2) shared-wrapping: we hold service keys and accept wrapped keys per-tenant (lower friction).

Attachment: kms_flow_notes.txt (high-level flow options).

Action items for triage meeting:
- Confirm which event types are 12-month (Tessa / Sarah)
- Product estimate for storage/query effort (Lauren)
- Eng rough estimate for BYOK pilot (Marcus)

I can join a 30-min sync tomorrow morning PST if that helps.

— Karthik
Senior Infrastructure PM

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intake: audit log sampling, retention buckets, and BYOK exception path

Thanks Karthik — good summary.

Triage proposal: we recommend an "exception + pilot" approach: approve a production BYOK pilot for a bounded tenant scope while we schedule a roadmap ticket for generalized retention buckets and on-demand export capability. That keeps Medivault compliant quickly while we build a reusable platform feature.

Lauren/Marcus: can you provide a rough MVP estimate (engineering weeks) for: 1) 365d retention for admin/audit events only, and 2) BYOK pilot (production-only, single-tenant). We’ll present these estimates to Medivault and propose a pilot SLA (180-day retention for pilot or full 365d?)

Sarah — we’ll propose a brief kickoff and a pilot scope doc once we have estimates.

Tessa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intake: audit log sampling, retention buckets, and BYOK exception path

Quick engineering readout:
- 365d retention (admin/audit events only): ~3-4 dev wks + 1 week infra rollout (storage lifecycle + query tagging). Risk: cost delta needs pricing hook.
- BYOK pilot (production, single tenant): MVP for wrapped-key flow (we accept tenant-wrapped keys, no HSM handover) ~4-6 dev wks + security review. Full client-held master key with HSM onboarding is a separate 8-12wk project.

Trade-offs: wrapped-key BYOK gives the legal protections many customers need while avoiding full HSM onboarding for the pilot. For audits that require proof of key custody, we need the wrapped-key logs and an attestation flow.

Attached: eng_estimates.xlsx (breakdown by effort and dependencies).

I’m marking this high priority but not blocking other roadmap commitments; we can open a short-term exception to support the pilot while roadmap work is scheduled.

— Marcus
Engineering Manager, Platform

1) Offer Medivault a pilot using wrapped-key BYOK for production (single tenant) + 365d admin/audit retention. Pilot SLA: 180-day initial commitment while we validate scale, then extend to 365d for the pilot tenant if no issues.
2) Product will open a roadmap ticket for generalized retention buckets and on-demand sampled export (Q3).
3) Legal/procurement: Tessa, can you coordinate updated SOW language and an exception letter? Sarah/procurement@medivault.com — we’ll share a pilot scope doc and a short SOW addendum. (Attachment: pilot_scope-180d.docx)

I’ll log this as an "exception-approved" case and schedule a 30-min kickoff with Medivault next week. Assigning action owners: Marcus: BYOK pilot eng tasks and eng_estimates.xlsx follow-up; Karthik: infra rollout timeline; Tessa: SOW + exception letter; Marissa: CS onboarding plan.

Sarah — if that works for you, I’ll propose times for a kickoff meeting and share a draft SOW within 48 hours.

Thanks — Lauren
